extra_quotes: Our methodology centers around the time evolution of the electronic density matrix, ˆρ(t), in the presence of an external perturbation, by solving the quantum Liouville equation, iℏ∂t ˆρ(t) = h ˆH(t), ˆρ(t) i [36].

To evaluate the trace in Eq. (1), we use the stochastic approximation [42, 50, 53]. For functions of the Hamiltonian, such as ˆU (t1, t0) and the Green’s functions entering the ˆLγ operator [34], instead of diagonalizing ˆH we employ the kernel polynomial method (KPM) and expand them as a series of Chebyshev polynomials [42, 50, 53].
